answer: After a gale, agents book telescopes beside an inlet to photograph a comet. The rental market charges a nonrefundable fee per telescope-minute reserved, prepaid before blocking the calendar; unpaid holds expire automatically. New accounts receive no free holding period. Splitting reservations among aliases cannot hoard viewing slots for free, since every blocked minute carries the same cost. This deters cheap sybil reservation attacks, though wealthy attackers can still pay to obstruct bookings.
